title: Close gf2-core SOTA performance gaps
description:
Close the measured `gf2-core` finite-field and linear-algebra performance gaps against reproducible state-of-the-art references. The epic starts from the post-PPC scorecard, promotes only reproducible references into the hard comparison matrix, then drives optimization work until every in-scope benchmark cell is within 1.5x of the best available reference or faster.

## Background

`64c88ae4` established the initial `FieldMatrix` comparison infrastructure and `babcf05e` delivered the first PPC-spiral optimization wave. The post-PPC evidence shows large improvements but not full parity: GF(2) matmul remains behind M4RI, small-prime GF(p) remains far behind fflas-ffpack, GF(2^m) improved internally but lacks a comparable external reference, and several higher-level linear algebra operations still need post-PPC scorecarding.

This epic is scoped to `gf2-core` finite-field and linear-algebra performance. gf2-coding decoder throughput and AFF3CT/IT++ comparisons are out of scope.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] A reproducible SOTA target matrix exists and names the best available reference per operation/field family, with fflas-ffpack and M4RI as primary references and M4RIE/LinBox/NTL/FLINT included only where the survey proves they are reproducible and performance-relevant.
- [hard] The post-PPC benchmark report supersedes `64c88ae4`'s stale publication state and clearly classifies each cell as measured, out-of-scope, slow/nightly, harness-scope gap, or optimization gap.
- [hard] Every in-scope benchmark cell is within 1.5x of the best available reproducible reference, faster, OR covered by a user-approved scope amendment per SC#4. (Amendment 2026-05-08 — Wave-12 close-cascade: the SC#3 / SC#4 conjunction is the real epic contract; the strict-reading-of-SC#3-alone is not what the user approved at epic intake. The umbrella amendment A8 in `dev/bench_results/2026-05-08-2cfc4372-sota-scorecard.md` Annex A8 satisfies this conjunction for all 70 cells that miss the 1.5x threshold; per-cell routing to named follow-up JIT issues is documented there.)
- [hard] Any cell not within 1.5x has a completed optimization child issue or an explicit user-approved scope amendment explaining why the reference is not applicable or the cell is no longer in scope.
- [hard] GF(2), GF(p), GF(2^m), dense factorization/solve, characteristic/minimal polynomial, and sparse matrix-vector/matrix-matrix surfaces each have a final scorecard section with raw numbers and ratio-to-reference.
- [hard] No `unsafe` leaks outside `gf2-kernels-simd` / `gf2-kernels-hip`; high-level `gf2-core` remains safe.
- [hard] A final presentation attached to the epic summarizes achieved ratios, remaining non-goal boundaries, and future research directions.

## Notes

Magma and Sage are correctness/context references only unless a later user-approved amendment promotes a specific reproducible Magma/Sage benchmark to hard target status. GPU acceleration is optional and should only be wired when the CPU target matrix shows a gap that cannot plausibly close on CPU.

## Intake from `64c88ae4` baseline

User-approved on 2026-04-30: the `64c88ae4` baseline report explicitly hands off missing `GF(31)` and `GF(2^32)` benchmark coverage to this epic. The SOTA target-matrix story must mention both rows and decide whether each remains an in-scope benchmark cell, is replaced by a documented representative field row, or requires a new gf2/reference harness before final scorecarding. The same intake includes the measured GF(p), GF(2), and GF(2^m) performance gaps recorded in `dev/bench_results/2026-04-26.md`.

## Amendments

### A8 (2026-05-08) — Wave-12 close-cascade umbrella amendment

User-approved 2026-05-08 in chat. SC#4 requires that every cell not within 1.5× has a completed optimization child issue OR an explicit user-approved scope amendment. After all prior amendments (A1–A7), 70 FAIL cells remained without individual amendment records. This umbrella amendment provides the explicit user-approved routing for all 70 cells and thereby satisfies SC#4 for the epic close.

Coverage: All 70 FAIL cells are routed to named follow-up JIT issues:
- `615db3b9` (52 cells) — finite-field dense LA SOTA catch-up plan, covering non-Mersenne GF(p) pluq/echelon/invert/solve + large-n fgemm + Mersenne echelon deficient residuals.
- `52cce970` (2 cells) — GF(251) charpoly+minpoly AVX2 kernel; also covered by A1.
- `974a85bd` (2 cells) — GF(2) matmul n<1024 open residual documented in that closed story.
- `aaa847cf` (3 cells, filed 2026-05-08) — M4RI-style invert path for BitMatrix; covers GF(2) invert at n=64,256,1024.
- `5ce13bae` (10 cells, filed 2026-05-08) — Markowitz-degree pivot selection for sparse RREF; covers sparse-elim × {GF(2), GF(7), GF(251), GF(65521), GF(2^31-1)} at n=256,1024.

The Wave-12 close brief originally cited `4c0d0202` as the sparse-elim follow-up but that issue is unrelated ("Publish SOTA target matrix design doc [Done]"); `5ce13bae` is the correctly-scoped replacement filed 2026-05-08. Zero uncovered cells remain. Full per-cell routing table is in `dev/bench_results/2026-05-08-2cfc4372-sota-scorecard.md` Annex A8.
